title: Getting Started as a Founder in Strawberry
description: Connect company reviews, meetings, growth, fundraising, and follow-through without rebuilding context for every decision.
introduction: A founder's day rarely respects functional boundaries. A customer conversation changes the product story. A hiring delay changes the plan. A board question sends you back through a spreadsheet, a meeting, and three Slack threads.

That is where Strawberry is most useful. The same companion can work across visible browser tabs, logged-in tools, meetings, messages, documents, dashboards, approved apps, and the public web. It can remember accepted context, so each good result can improve the next one instead of disappearing into another isolated chat.

sections.title: See the whole Founder Operating System

blocks.text: You do not need to configure the whole system before Strawberry becomes useful. Bring the company work that matters now. Your companion can recommend a few relevant starting points and help finish one reviewable piece while keeping the wider company picture in view.

rows: Prepare for the day and important conversations, then preserve the decisions and commitments that follow.
Reconcile changed priorities, risks, ownership, and material pipeline exceptions, then shape the accepted view for leadership or the board.
Connect market and customer evidence to growth, fundraising, hiring, and the decisions that change the plan.
Turn a founder's accepted method into shared context, a team workflow, or a Routine only after it works.

items.context: Choose and complete the founder workflow that would help most right now.

blocks.text: A daily brief can surface the meetings, messages, commitments, and decisions that deserve attention. Meeting preparation can gather the context that might change a conversation; a reliable transcript or set of notes can carry the decisions and follow-through into the next step.

When you need a broader company view, Strawberry can reconcile commitments across the systems where work happens and show what changed, what is blocked, where ownership is unclear, and which decisions need you. Use that once or within a cadence you already have; do not invent a weekly review. Keep source links, conflicts, and gaps visible, then turn only the accepted picture into a leadership or board update.

items.context: See which meetings, messages, commitments, risks, and decisions deserve attention today.
Prepare for a leadership, board, customer, or partner conversation using context that could change it.
Reconcile commitments and produce an exception and ownership view when one would help.
Turn the accepted company picture into a concise leadership or board update.

sections.title: Build the company with specialist judgment

blocks.text: Founders touch every function, but they do not need a founder-specific copy of every workflow. Strawberry can route customer growth to Sales judgment, hiring to Recruiting, market evidence to Research, and follow-through to Operations while the founder keeps the company decision.

rows: Find and calibrate customers, research priority accounts, then prepare grounded outreach.
Reconcile the story with traction, build a first investor set, prepare the needed materials, and plan the near-term process.
Map the market or analyze competitors before turning approved evidence into a brief or deck.
Use the Recruiting system for the search and Operations when someone is ready to join.

blocks.text: Context can continue across these handoffs. A market map can sharpen the first customer set; customer and product evidence can strengthen a fundraising story. The goal of raising still does not grant permission to contact investors, share materials, or expose a data room.

items.context: Build and correct a small, qualified customer set before widening the search.
Prepare an evidence-backed story, first investor list, and practical near-term process.
Understand the market, account universe, whitespace, concentration, and evidence behind a company decision.
Choose the right hiring workflow, from defining the role through interview decisions and pipeline review.

sections.title: Turn a good run into a company rhythm

blocks.text: Treat early work as a draft you can coach. Correct the sources, priorities, assumptions, depth, voice, and review points. Strawberry can remember the accepted method, so the next run starts with what the company learned rather than a blank prompt.

Share the approved result when someone needs the artifact. Set up a shared workflow when the team needs the same inputs, ownership, destination, privacy boundaries, and review behavior. Add a Routine only when the method is trusted and the cadence or trigger is real. That is how a useful first result becomes a Founder Operating System without creating another layer of administration.

items.context: Turn a proven founder workflow into a shared method with clear ownership and boundaries.
